questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: The alpha helix and beta pleated sheet represent which level of protein structure?
options: Secondary structure, stabilised by hydrogen bonds
questions.concept: Primary structure is the amino acid sequence, tertiary the three-dimensional fold stabilised by disulphide, hydrophobic and ionic interactions, and quaternary the assembly of multiple subunits.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Collagen is unique in containing high amounts of:
options: Glycine at every third residue, with hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine
questions.concept: Glycine's small size permits the tight triple helix. Hydroxylation of proline and lysine requires vitamin C, so scurvy produces unstable collagen with bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Type I collagen is the predominant collagen of:
questions.concept: Type II is in cartilage, type III is reticulin, and type IV forms basement membrane and is the target in Goodpasture and Alport syndromes. Type I defects cause osteogenesis imperfecta.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Sickle cell haemoglobin results from substitution at position 6 of the beta chain of:
questions.concept: Replacing a charged residue with a hydrophobic one creates a sticky patch causing polymerisation on deoxygenation. HbC results from lysine substitution at the same position.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Haemoglobin exhibits a sigmoid oxygen dissociation curve because of:
options: Cooperative binding between its four subunits
questions.concept: Myoglobin with a single haem shows a hyperbolic curve and higher affinity, making it a tissue oxygen store rather than a transporter. Cooperativity is what allows efficient loading and unloading.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate lowers haemoglobin oxygen affinity by:
options: Binding the central cavity of deoxyhaemoglobin and stabilising the T state
questions.concept: HbF binds 2,3-BPG poorly because gamma chains lack key binding residues, giving it higher affinity and enabling placental oxygen transfer from maternal blood.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Methaemoglobin differs from normal haemoglobin in that iron is:
options: In the ferric state and cannot bind oxygen
questions.concept: Cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen with chocolate-brown blood is characteristic. Methylene blue is the antidote, but is ineffective and dangerous in G6PD deficiency where ascorbic acid is used.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Denaturation of a protein involves:
options: Loss of higher-order structure with retention of the primary sequence
questions.concept: Heat, extremes of pH, urea and detergents disrupt non-covalent interactions. The classic demonstration is the heat coagulation test for urinary protein, where albumin denatures on boiling.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Prion diseases result from:
options: Conformational conversion of a normal alpha-helical protein into a beta-sheet-rich infectious form
questions.concept: The abnormal PrP-Sc is protease-resistant and templates conversion of normal protein, causing Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease and kuru. It resists standard sterilisation, a major concern for surgical instruments.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Electrophoresis separates haemoglobin variants on the basis of:
options: Charge and molecular size at a given pH
questions.concept: HbS moves more slowly than HbA towards the anode because it has lost a negative charge. HPLC has largely replaced electrophoresis for accurate quantification in thalassaemia and sickle screening.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Transcription in eukaryotes producing messenger RNA is carried out by:
questions.concept: Polymerase I makes ribosomal RNA and III transfer RNA. Alpha-amanitin from Amanita phalloides specifically inhibits polymerase II, which is why mushroom poisoning causes fulminant hepatic failure.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Post-transcriptional processing of eukaryotic mRNA includes:
options: 5' capping, 3' polyadenylation and splicing out of introns
questions.concept: Alternative splicing lets one gene encode multiple proteins, and splicing mutations cause disease - beta thalassaemia frequently results from splice site mutations rather than deletions.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: The genetic code is described as degenerate because:
options: Most amino acids are encoded by more than one codon
One codon codes for several amino acids
questions.concept: Degeneracy is mostly in the third base (wobble position), so third-base substitutions are often silent. This buffers the effect of point mutations.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: A frameshift mutation results from:
options: Insertion or deletion of nucleotides not in multiples of three
questions.concept: Frameshifts alter every downstream codon and usually create a premature stop, producing a severely truncated protein - which is why Duchenne dystrophy from frameshift deletions is far more severe than in-frame Becker deletions.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: A nonsense mutation is one that:
options: Converts an amino acid codon into a stop codon
questions.concept: Missense changes one amino acid as in sickle cell disease, silent mutations change nothing, and nonsense mutations truncate the protein, typically causing complete loss of function.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Diphtheria toxin inhibits protein synthesis by:
questions.concept: A single toxin molecule can kill a cell, explaining its extraordinary potency. Pseudomonas exotoxin A acts by the same mechanism, while ricin depurinates ribosomal RNA.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Post-translational modifications include all EXCEPT:
questions.concept: Splicing is post-transcriptional, occurring on RNA. Vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors and vitamin C-dependent hydroxylation of collagen are clinically important post-translational steps.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Reverse transcriptase is characteristic of:
options: Retroviruses, synthesising DNA from an RNA template
questions.concept: It is the target of zidovudine and nevirapine in HIV therapy and lacks proofreading, giving a high mutation rate that drives drug resistance and frustrates vaccine development.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: Southern, Northern and Western blotting detect respectively:
questions.concept: SNOW DROP is the mnemonic - Southern, Northern, Western for DNA, RNA, Protein. Western blot was the traditional confirmatory HIV test, and Southern blot detects trinucleotide repeat expansions.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.stem: The polymerase chain reaction requires all EXCEPT:
questions.concept: Reverse transcriptase is needed only for RT-PCR when starting from RNA, as in viral load testing. Standard PCR needs template, primers, Taq polymerase, dNTPs and thermal cycling.
